entry.title: Enabling Google Cast Support on a Samsung Q800A Soundbar
entry.content:
Links: codon.org.uk | lobsters

Matthew Garrett detailed a technical process for enabling Google Cast support on a US-model Samsung Q800A soundbar, which lacks the feature natively despite its presence on Australian variants. By extracting the firmware from a secondhand unit's eMMC storage, he identified a hidden Samsung Debug Bridge (sdb) interface that could be activated via network and USB configurations.

Once root access was established, he bypassed regional restrictions by altering the system country code, manually provisioning cryptographic keys into the soundbar's Trustzone environment, and updating the setup configuration endpoint. While the modification successfully exposed the device to local Cast clients, the regional configuration mismatch caused conflicts with SmartThings home integration.

entry.title: Unredacted 1964 FBI Letter to Martin Luther King Jr. Examined by Historians
entry.content:
Links: vox.com | nytimes.com | hacker news

In 1964, top FBI officials sent an anonymous, threatening letter and surveillance recordings of extramarital affairs to civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. in an effort to compel him to commit suicide. Directed by William Sullivan under FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover, the blackmail campaign followed years of intense government monitoring designed to discredit King's leadership and activism.

Yale historian Beverly Gage later unearthed a fully unredacted version of the document from archival records, revealing details previously concealed by government redactions. The text explicitly derided King's honors, including his Nobel Peace Prize, and warned him that he had 34 days to take his own life, highlighting the severe abuses of domestic intelligence agencies during the civil rights era.
